reels.title: 3 Historical Vampire Graves That Defied Science
facts: In 2014, archaeologists at Drawsko, Poland documented multiple 17th-century burials with iron sickles placed across throats.
A female skeleton excavated in 2022 in Pien, Poland was buried with a padlock on her toe and a sickle neck-restraint.
Calmet published Traite sur les apparitions des esprits et sur les vampires in 1751 documenting Balkan burial exhumations.
The 1344 Czech chronicle of Neplach records shepherd Myslata being staked through the heart to cease nocturnal attacks.
Venice island of Lazzaretto Nuovo yielded a 16th-century plague mass burial containing a woman with a brick forced into her jaw.
reels.hook: Iron sickles locked across their throats

beats.text: 5 · 1751: Dom Calmet documents official Balkan vampire exhumations
4 · 1344: Czech chronicles record staking shepherd Myslata's corpse
3 · Venice: A 16th-century plague skull wedged with brick
2 · Drawsko, Poland: 17th-century graves with throat sickles
1 · Pien, 2022: Female burial with padlock and neck-blade

reels.caption: Iron sickles locked across severed throats. Padlocked toes buried deep in Polish soil. Bricks forced into the jaws of plague victims in Venetian mass graves. These were not superstitions whispered in darkness. They were state-sanctioned burial rites meant to bind the restless dead to their earth. The historical record confirms what folklore tried to conceal. Which burial shocks you most: 1, 2, or 3? Read the accounts at alloccult.com/death-afterlife/vampirology.

review_log.summary: All segments present historically accurate archaeological and documented cases of anti-vampiric burial rites across Europe (Pień, Drawsko, Venice, Neplach's chronicle, and Calmet's 1751 treatise). The imagery and historical citations align well with source records.

reels.title: 3 Darkest Secrets of the Goetia
facts: Harley MS 6483 in the British Library contains the earliest complete English copy of the Ars Goetia dating to 1712.
Demon number 1, Bael, appears with three heads: a toad, a man, and a cat, commanding 66 legions.
The vessel described in the Lemegeton was made of brass and sealed with lead bearing the secret seal of Solomon.
Wierus cataloged 69 spirits earlier in the 1577 appendix Pseudomonarchia Daemonum before Mathers translated 72.
Demon number 32, Asmoday, confers the ring of virtutes and teaches arithmetic, astronomy, and geometry.
reels.hook: King Solomon bound 72 spirits in brass

reels.title: 3 Gematria Numbers Tied to Occult Death
facts: In Hebrew gematria, Maveth (Death, Mem-Vau-Tav) computes to a numerical value of 446.
The number 666 appears in Revelation 13:18 as the number of the Beast, calculating to Nero Caesar in Hebrew spelling NRON QSR.
The Zohar, authored in Castile in the late 13th century, asserts letters are the literal structural blocks of creation.
Cordovero's Pardes Rimonim (1548) details the system of Temurah and the 231 gates of letter transposition from Sefer Yetzirah.
The angel of death Samael (Samekh-Mem-Aleph-Lamed) totals 131 in classic mispar hekhrechi reckoning.
reels.hook: Numbers conceal the names of the damned

beats.text: 5 · Letters form the structural fabric of reality
4 · Cordovero mapped the 231 gates of transposition
3 · The number 131 spells the poison angel Samael
2 · The value 446 calculates the Hebrew Maveth death
1 · The Beast 666 encodes the emperor Nron Qsr

reels.caption:
Numbers conceal the names of the damned.

In Hebrew gematria, letters are not symbols. They are the architecture of existence.

reels.title: 4 Blood Covenants from Real Witchcraft Trials
facts: The 1634 trial of Father Urbain Grandier in Loudun produced a Latin contract purportedly signed by Lucifer, Asmodeus, and Leviathan.
Grandier's pact is preserved in the Bibliotheque nationale de France, cataloged under French manuscript archives.
King James VI of Scotland published Daemonologie in 1597 describing bodily marks given by the Devil as signatures of fealty.
The Malleus Maleficarum (1486/87, Heinrich Kramer) made the pact with the Devil central to its definition of witchcraft; it was a treatise, not a law code.
In March 1692 at Salem, Tituba confessed to making her mark in the Devil's book.
reels.hook: Contracts with the Devil survive in archives

beats.text: 4 · 1487: The Malleus puts the Devil's pact at witchcraft's heart
3 · 1597: King James VI calls the Devil's mark his seal
2 · 1692: At Salem, Tituba confesses to signing the Devil's book
1 · 1634: Grandier's 'pact', signed by demons, survives in Paris

reels.caption:
Contracts with the Devil survive in archives.
At Loudun in 1634, a 'pact' bearing the names of Lucifer, Asmodeus and Leviathan was used against the priest Urbain Grandier. He was burned. The document is still in Paris.
Courts across Europe treated the Devil's pact as real evidence.
